idiom_name: enum with associated values + switch interpreter
implementation_notes: Swift enums are sum types: one `enum Op` with associated values holds the described effects and `switch` deconstructs them with compiler-proven coverage - no visitor, and a new case breaks every interpreter. Operations are value types, so programs are immutable and `Equatable` (synthesized when payloads are), which makes test assertions trivial. Where several runtimes must be substituted (live, preview, tests), put the switch behind a `protocol Interpreter { func run(_ op: Op) async throws -> Value }`; `async/await` and `Task` belong inside the interpreter, since calling an async function executes it.
pitfalls: Recursive enums need `indirect` (or an explicit box), which heap-allocates every payload node.
Enums with associated values are only `Equatable` when their payloads are, and cannot be `CaseIterable`: a closure or class payload silently removes value equality from programs.
Adding a case to a public enum is source-breaking for client switches (library evolution may require `@unknown default`), so version algebras that ship across module boundaries.
